scope: Final peer audit of the three HU draft decisions and their root scope review; no source rerun, registry mutation, or new semantic evidence.

binding_checks.finding: The question is scoped to the Iteration 12 repeated e/i proposal. It explicitly limits GDT626's terminal a+i*n minim parser and does not export it to all e-runs. The outcome preserves scalar, phonetic, inflectional and abbreviation rivals; 686's axis choice is correctly described as renderer policy rather than universal semantic rejection.

The draft keeps the early N2/SET VALUE assignment proposal separate from the later GDT626 III convention. It correctly treats N2 versus III as a counting/segmentation offset and does not infer an imperative D or a universal D+host rule from line-entry skew.

The draft identifies the four-channel builder and validator as a deterministic authored classification with 19 mapped signs and three dormant running signs. It does not claim a universal-axis rejection or a single rival interpretation; it retains selector, delimiter and subtype alternatives and limits the result to a source/contract audit.

evidence_validation.method: Every evidence array in all three draft decisions was checked with tools.semantic_identity._evidence against its typed path, contiguous line span, quote and SHA.

remaining_boundary: The three decisions are scoped assessments of source contracts and formal patterns. None supplies an independent assignment/value binding, universal e/i semantic axis, or independently decoded local-channel meaning. Their reopening criteria correctly require a specified rival with a different scoreable prediction and source-bound held support.
